content: The 1998 Klang Valley water crisis occurred in Malaysia in February 1998. This crisis was triggered by a significant drop in water levels at three major reservoir dams in the Klang Valley: the Klang Gates Dam, Batu Dam, and Semenyih Dam. The reduction in water levels was attributed to the El Niño phenomenon. As a result of this water shortage, nearly all residents in the Klang Valley were affected. The situation became so severe that the government had to implement water rationing measures. These measures were introduced prior to the 1998 Commonwealth Games, which were held in Kuala Lumpur. Although the water shortage was officially blamed on El Niño, the actual rainfall data from the months leading up to February 1998 in Wilayah Persekutuan (Federal Territory) did not show a significant deviation from average levels. In fact, in November 1997, the Empangan Genting Klang (Genting Klang reservoir) recorded its highest-ever rainfall. Similarly, in October 1997, the Kajang station, located near the Semenyih Dam, also experienced its highest recorded rainfall.
